threads.title: The clerk in grey at the winch-house: an older man with a desk on two kegs who writes the Confessors' letters and never kneels at the dawn bell; he gave the almoner two slivers before the snow and called them the Spire's mercy for the wounded
threads.who_knows: Anselm (he saw him); Darrow, Hollis, Maelis, Wren and the Prior have it from Anselm's confession (04:s1); the reader. Marrant knows his own clerk. The clerk's name is not on the page

note: Ch4 slot 2 (b1.4): the lever on the page: Mirren's letter in the clerk's hand (= the hand on Aldric's letters' direction: T3 plant, Vane's secretary, unnamed), a lock of dark hair; Anselm reads and does not weep ('That's his word'). kept_off: Vane's name on the hand (the reader may join it: 'the same hand as the direction on his brother's letters'); the forty-one; what the clerk is; Marrant himself (mentioned only).

The mare is held till the thaw on his name. Rae is in the House tonight and goes down at first light; she has not said where she saw the hand. Anselm holds the key and his sister's hair.
